stories.title: Tech Firms Ink Full-Floor Leases with Moinian Group
stories.excerpt: The Moinian Group has signed approximately 26,000 square feet of new office leases at 245 Fifth Ave. in Manhattan’s Midtown South neighborhood. The two full-floor transactions follow more than 95,000 square feet of leases previously announced at the property. The newly signed leases include: Sona Technologies: Leased approximately 12,000 square feet. Represented by Evan Kleinberg and Lenny Kohlmayer of Cornelia Street Partner. Blacksmith Software: Leased approximately 14,000 square feet. Represented by the Tandem Space Team. “245 Fifth Ave. continues to attract a diverse mix of businesses seeking high-quality office space in one of Manhattan’s most dynamic commercial neighborhoods,” said Omar Sozkesen, VP of Commercial Leasing at The Moinian Group. “These transactions reflect strong demand in the building and the strength of its location, flexible floor plates and distinctive character.” The Moinian Group was represented by Scott Klau, Erik Harris and Ben Klau of Newmark in all transaction The post Tech Firms Ink Full-Floor Leases with Moinian Group appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tech firms lease 26,000 SF full floors at 245 Fifth Ave, Manhattan Midtown South
Follows 95,000 SF previously announced; property attracts diverse business mix
Strong office demand signals in prime NYC commercial submarket
stories.summary: Moinian Group has signed two full-floor tech leases totaling 26,000 SF at 245 Fifth Ave in Midtown South, following 95,000 SF of earlier leases at the same property. The transaction reflects sustained demand for quality office space in one of Manhattan's most dynamic neighborhoods, with the property's flexible floor plates and distinctive character cited as key attractions. Office demand remains resilient in prime Manhattan submarkets despite macro headwinds.
stories.impact: Persistent office leasing in Manhattan's Midtown South—especially to tech tenants—sustains employment and population density in the core, underpinning baseline apartment demand. However, this signals stabilization, not expansion; multifamily developers should monitor whether tech hiring continues or stalls, as office leasing is a lagging indicator of job growth. No immediate development catalyst here, but a sign that white-collar employment remains anchored to Manhattan.

stories.title: Pasadena Offices Sell for Residential Conversion
stories.excerpt: NAI Capital Commercial EVPs John S. Archibald and Guillermo Olaiz, alongside senior associate Stephen Lam of the Investment Services Group in the Pasadena office, represented the seller, Star Horizon, LLC, in the sale of ZK Plaza, a 41,586-square-foot office building in Pasadena. The property sold for $13,400,000, representing a 3.5% premium over asking. Located at 600 N. Rosemead Blvd., ZK Plaza occupies a 2.12-acre site in East Pasadena, directly across from General Motors’ advanced design center. Originally built in 1966, the two-story office building was expanded in 1989 and renovated in 2011. Elysian Housing, LLC, plans to redevelop the site into a 133-unit affordable housing community, adaptively reusing the existing office building for 51 units and constructing a new five-story building with 82 units. Archibald said, “This transaction highlights the opportunities for well-located properties in established Southern California markets. ZK Plaza’s location in East Pasadena, near major employers and transportation, offers significant potential for its next chapter.” The post Pasadena Offices Sell for Residential Conversion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 41,586 SF office building (ZK Plaza) sells for $13.4M in East Pasadena
Elysian Housing plans 133-unit affordable housing conversion: 51 adaptive-reuse, 82 new construction
Site near GM advanced design center and transit; sold at 3.5% premium to asking
stories.summary: ZK Plaza, a two-story office building in East Pasadena, sold for $13.4 million (3.5% premium over asking) to Elysian Housing, which plans a 133-unit affordable housing redevelopment. The project will adaptively reuse the existing 41,586 SF office structure for 51 units and construct a new five-story building with 82 units on the 2.12-acre site across from GM's design center. The location near major employers and transit is driving opportunistic office-to-residential conversion.
stories.impact: East Pasadena's proximity to GM's advanced design center and regional transit creates stable demand for workforce housing. Elysian's 133-unit conversion signals that office-to-multifamily arbitrage remains viable in Los Angeles submarkets with embedded employment anchors and zoning flexibility. For TCR: monitor similar conversion opportunities in LA submarkets with obsolete suburban office stock and strong employment clusters; the 3.5% premium sale price indicates sellers recognize adaptive-reuse value, compressing acquisition margins but signaling market confidence.

stories.title: Lightstone Capital Provides $29.5M Loan for Orange, N.J., Multifamily Development
stories.excerpt: Orange, N.J.-based PEEK Capital, a division of multifamily developer and operator PEEK Properties, has secured a $29.5 million bridge loan on its recently completed multifamily project in Orange known as the Lincoln, Commercial Observer has learned. The bridge loan was provided by Lightstone Group’s real estate debt platform, Lightstone Capital. Daniel Cohen of Ackman-Ziff advised on the transaction. “Peek Properties is a best-in-class sponsor, and Lightstone executed flawlessly on this pre-stabilization bridge loan, which allowed Peek to repatriate equity early in the leasing process,” Cohen told CO in a statement. The loan will support the 102-unit building’s continued lease-up and stabilization, as well as refinance the property’s previous construction financing. Peek previously secured a $20.5 million loan for the development from Amboy Bank in 2024, Real Estate NJ reported. The five-story, full-block apartment building at 407 Highland Avenue in Orange received its final certificate of occupancy in September, according to Lightstone Capital, and has begun leasing a range of one- and two-bedroom residences. “Newly built multifamily properties with proven sponsorship track records have always presented attractive lending opportunities as they transition towards stabilization,” Eugene Rozovsky, senior managing director at Lightstone Capital, said in a statement. The property’s location is one black from N.J. Transit’s Highland Avenue station, offering access to Newark and Midtown Manhattan’s Pennsylvania Station. The cities of Orange and East Orange have been a popular site of luxury apartment development for several years, as renters are priced out of New York City. “The Lincoln continues to attract strong interest from prospective residents, and this refinancing marks an important milestone in the life cycle of the property,” Philip J. bullets: PEEK Properties secures $29.5M bridge loan from Lightstone Capital for Lincoln, Orange, N.J.
102-unit, five-story building achieved final CO in September; under lease-up and stabilization
Previous $20.5M construction loan from Amboy Bank in 2024; bridge refinances and funds lease-up
stories.summary: PEEK Capital (PEEK Properties) closed a $29.5 million bridge loan from Lightstone Capital for the Lincoln, a recently completed 102-unit multifamily project in Orange, N.J. The five-story, full-block building received its certificate of occupancy in September and is in active lease-up. The bridge replaces prior $20.5 million construction financing from Amboy Bank and supports stabilization. Bridge terms and rate not disclosed.
stories.impact: New Jersey multifamily financing remains active and accessible for lease-up stabilization at completion. Orange's urban infill location and robust early leasing support bridge deployment; the quick turnaround to bridge (COO Sept., bridge closed within weeks) suggests strong lender appetite and sponsor credibility. For TCR in New Jersey metros (Jersey City, Newark, Orange submarkets): recent-delivery projects with solid absorption can access bridge capital efficiently, enabling equity return cycles and reducing hold-time risk. Monitor Orange's lease-up pace—strong metrics here validate the submarket as viable for TCR acquisition or development.

stories.title: AJ Capital Partners Lands $52M Refi for Princeton, N.J., Hotel
stories.excerpt: AJ Capital Partners secured a round of financing for one of its hospitality properties in New Jersey, Commercial Observer has learned. GreenOak (formerly BGO) originated a $52 million loan for the 180-room hotel in Princeton, N.J., known as the Graduate by Hilton Princeton, according to sources familiar with the deal. The hotel property at 10 Chambers Street sits directly across from Princeton University. The financing comes with a three-year term and two 12-month extension options, the source said. CBRE’s Tom Rugg, Tom Traynor and Henry Fenmore arranged the financing, but the brokerage declined to comment. GreenOak and AJ Capital did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The hotel, which opened in 2024, is part of AJ Capital’s line of 33 properties known as Graduate Hotels that are near major higher education facilities in both the U.S. and U.K. The Nashville-based real estate firm owns hospitality properties all over the globe, including Wedgewood Village south of Downtown Nashville in the famous music city, as well as Marine & Lawn Golf Hotels, which operates Marine & Lawn Rusacks in St. Andrews, Scotland. The Princeton deal closed on the heels of AJ Capital landing a $62.5 million loan in late August from Peachtree Group to refinance its Graduate by Hilton Nashville hotel property near Vanderbilt University, CO first reported at the time. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: AJ Capital Partners closes $52M refinance for 180-room Graduate by Hilton Princeton
GreenOak (formerly BGO) originated loan; 3-year term plus two 1-year extension options
Hotel opened 2024, located across from Princeton University; part of 33-property Graduate Hotels portfolio
stories.summary: AJ Capital Partners secured a $52 million refinance from GreenOak for the Graduate by Hilton Princeton, a 180-room hotel that opened in 2024. The property is located directly across from Princeton University and is part of AJ Capital's Graduate Hotels brand (33 properties nationally near major universities). The loan carries a three-year term with two 12-month extension options.
stories.impact: Hospitality financing, not multifamily; limited relevance to apartment development. However, the success of Graduate Hotels—a portfolio strategy anchored to university towns—suggests strong demand for visitor/transient lodging near major institutions. This may reduce opportunity for purpose-built student housing in Princeton and similar college towns, or indicate that experiential retail/hotel uses compete for prime university-adjacent real estate that multifamily developers might otherwise target.

stories.title: Financial Tech Platform Intuit Takes 4K SF at the Orchard in LIC
stories.excerpt: The Orchard, Queens’ tallest residential tower, has signed several new retail leases totaling 7,468 square feet, building owner and developer BLDG Management announced Thursday. In September, financial services platform Intuit, the company behind programs including TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma and Mailchimp, signed a 3,546-square-foot lease at the 70-story property at 42-06 Orchard Street in Queens’ Long Island City neighborhood. “The Orchard was designed to be more than a place to live, with residences, amenities and services that give people opportunities to live, work and connect right at home,” Lloyd Goldman, president of BLDG Management, said in a statement. “BLDG has been part of the Long Island City community for more than 60 years, and we wanted the Orchard to build on that legacy by creating a place that serves both residents and the broader neighborhood.” The asking rent and the length of Intuit’s lease were not disclosed. The average asking rent for retail space in Long Island City ranges between $18 and $100 per square foot, according to listings on Loopnet.com. Intuit is expected to open its Orchard location in December. In October, Japanese tea and beverage brand Mollytea also signed a new 1,671-square-foot lease at 42-06 Orchard Street, and is expected to open in the second quarter of 2027. The asking rent and the length of the lease were not disclosed. In July, Korean beauty supplier Tokimo took 2,251 square feet at the Orchard for what will be its third location in the greater metropolitan area. Tokimo also has locations in Flushing and East Rutherford, N.J. The asking rent and the length of the lease were not disclosed. Broker information was not immediately available. Corcoran Sunshine is the exclusive marketing and leasing agent for the Orchard. The building houses 824 residences and is 90 percent leased, according to BLDG. bullets: Intuit leases 3,546 SF at the Orchard, Queens' 70-story residential tower in LIC
Multiple retail tenants signed 7,468 SF total; average asking rent $18–$100/SF in LIC
Reflects live-work-play trend; building designed with residences, amenities, and services integrated
stories.summary: The Orchard, a 70-story residential tower at 42-06 Orchard Street in Long Island City, Queens, signed a 3,546 SF retail lease with Intuit (TurboTax, QuickBooks, Mailchimp) and several other retail tenants totaling 7,468 SF. The project was intentionally designed to integrate work and living amenities on-site. Retail asking rents in LIC range $18–$100/SF.
stories.impact: LIC multifamily market is maturing: build-to-suit mixed-use towers can now support brand-name tech tenants seeking small local offices, reversing the flight-to-midtown trend. This signals LIC's appeal as a secondary office hub with lower rents and younger demographics than Manhattan—supporting both residential absorption and workplace diversity. For TCR: co-tenanted residential with embedded retail and office can command premium rents; consider office-retail integration in future LIC and similar secondary markets (Astoria, Williamsburg) as cost-competitive alternatives to Manhattan draw talent and employees.

stories.title: Miami Gardens Leases Public Land for Proposed Hotel
stories.excerpt: The city of Miami Gardens, Fla., this week approved a land lease that sets up the development of a 127-room hotel on city-owned land near Hard Rock Stadium. The proposal calls for a 127-room hotel, the Beckham Hotel Miami Gardens, and a parking garage on part of a 3.5-acre parcel. The hotel – no brand affiliation has been announced yet – and parking garage will be adjacent to a new performing arts center the city plans at the same site. The Beckham in question is not related to soccer star David Beckham. The project is led by Phillip L. Beckham III, a Black developer from Chicago. The city of Miami Gardens, population 116,115, is 59 percent Black, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. “We invest in communities that look like us,” Beckham told the City Council during a meeting this week. The Miami Gardens’ City Council voted unanimously to approve a lease of city-owned vacant property at 18600 Northwest 25th Avenue to P3 Markets and Beckham Hospitality. The deal calls for the developer to pay the city about $18.6 million in rent over the 50-year lease. City documents said the new hotel would be part of a larger project that includes a second hotel and a performing arts center with a 1,200-seat theater. The site is two miles from Hard Rock Stadium, home of the Miami Dolphins, the University of Miami Hurricanes, the annual Orange Bowl, a Formula 1 race and the Miami Open tennis tournament. Billionaire Stephen Ross owns that property and the Dolphins. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Miami Gardens approves 50-year land lease for 127-room hotel near Hard Rock Stadium
Developer Phillip L. Beckham III (Chicago-based Black developer); $18.6M total rent over 50 years
City population 116,115 (59% Black); project includes performing arts center on adjacent city land
stories.summary: The Miami Gardens City Council unanimously approved a land lease with Beckham Hospitality and P3 Markets for a 127-room hotel (Beckham Hotel Miami Gardens) and parking garage on city-owned land near Hard Rock Stadium. The developer, Phillip L. Beckham III, a Black real estate entrepreneur from Chicago, will pay Miami Gardens approximately $18.6 million in total rent over 50 years. The hotel site is adjacent to a new performing arts center also planned by the city.
stories.impact: Hospitality financing and community development, not multifamily; minimal direct relevance. However, the performing arts center and hotel complex signal Miami Gardens' investment in destination/experiential amenities near Hard Rock Stadium, potentially lifting population and visitor traffic. For TCR: monitor whether this catalyzes residential development nearby (workforce housing, market-rate apartments for hotel/entertainment workers); Hard Rock events and stadium-adjacent activation can drive local multifamily demand in underutilized Miami Gardens submarket.

stories.title: Hudson Valley Boutique Shop Signs Lease in Manhattan’s Nolita
stories.excerpt: A Beacon, N.Y., knickknack shop is making its New York City debut with a store in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. Solstad House General Store signed a five-year, 1,200-square-foot lease at Emmanuel Stark’s 167 Mott Street, with an asking rent of $6,750 per month, according to broker Meridian Retail Leasing. “We reached out to Solstad House directly because we thought the space was a perfect fit for their brand, and they moved fast,” Meridian’s Carson Shahrabani said in a statement. “We went from first email to a signed lease in about two weeks, and they’ll be open for the holidays.” Meridian’s Shahrabani, Noam Aziz and Michael Escava represented both the landlord and tenant in the transaction. “[Solstad House] already has a loyal following in Beacon, and a lot of those customers live in Manhattan,” Aziz said in a statement. “This store gives them a home in the city.” Solstad House primarily sells home goods, food items, puzzles, personal care products and clothing, according to its website. Stark purchased the property between Broome and Grand streets from Platinum Properties for $17 million in 2015. The seven-story building has 26 residential units and two retail units spanning between 500 and 600 square feet on the ground floor, not including cellars, according to CO coverage at the time and property records. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Solstad House General Store (Beacon, N.Y.) signs 5-year, 1,200 SF lease in Manhattan Nolita
Asking rent $6,750/month ($67.50/SF annually); leased by Emmanuel Stark at 167 Mott Street
Merchants fast-tracked from first email to signed lease in two weeks; opening for holidays
stories.summary: Solstad House General Store, a boutique retailer from Beacon, N.Y., signed a five-year, 1,200 SF retail lease at 167 Mott Street in Manhattan's Nolita neighborhood for $6,750/month ($67.50/SF/year). The deal closed in two weeks from initial contact. Solstad House sells home goods, food, puzzles, and apparel; the opening targets the holidays and a customer base already living in Manhattan who patronized the Beacon location.
stories.impact: Retail leasing, not multifamily; no direct development impact. However, the speed of lease closure and Nolita's continued retail resilience signal healthy retail markets in dense Manhattan neighborhoods with strong residential base. No constraint on multifamily fundamentals; retail activation reinforces residential value in prime neighborhoods.
